name: Cryptic crossword No 22,582
preamble: Mercury (Ken Guy), who died suddenly on 29 June, compiled for the paper for over 20 years. This is his last puzzle.

clue.text: Prepare for the ice-dancing - and hurry!

blocks.note: first meaning: literally, put on the boots with blades before going on the rink
second meaning: an informal urging to get a move on

explanation.surface: A coach tells a late skater to get ready for the ice-dance and be quick about it.
explanation.walkthrough: The literal phrase is also an idiom telling someone to move faster.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiomatic command urges someone to speed up, while its literal sense describes readying blades before skating.

clue.text: Squad inside pipe is making good progress

indicators.note: inside tells us the squad sits within the word for pipe

blocks.note: a squad is a team
to pipe is to sing, as a bird does

explanation.surface: A team of plumbers is getting on well with a pipe job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pipe' looks like a noun for plumbing, but it is the verb for a bird's song.
explanation.definitionFit: Steaming ahead, like a fast locomotive, describes moving quickly and advancing well on a task.

clue.text: Wood with bad smell in East New York

indicators.note: in places the smell between the letters standing for the city

blocks.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east
BO is body odour
standard abbreviation for the city

explanation.surface: Some timber in East New York gives off an unpleasant odour.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebony is a dense dark hardwood from tropical trees, prized for piano keys and carving.

clue.text: Religious believer, a learned cleric, in bus hit after turning

indicators.note: turning suggests the letters of the vehicle and the blow being twisted into a new order
in puts the cleric inside the rearranged letters of the other words

blocks.note: DD is Doctor of Divinity, a learned churchman
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A scholarly churchman is caught in a bus crash after the vehicle turns.
explanation.walkthrough: BUS and HIT are rearranged, then DD goes into the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A Buddhist is a follower of the teachings of the Buddha, so an adherent of a faith.

clue.text: Implored rest to take something to eat

indicators.note: the word for rest takes in, or holds, the food item

blocks.note: a bed is where you rest
an egg is a food

explanation.surface: Someone pleaded with a patient to stop resting and have a bite.
explanation.definitionFit: To beg is to plead or entreat earnestly, so both past tenses mean asked desperately.

clue.text: Sign on holiday island: "Firm requires sailors"

blocks.note: Capri is an Italian resort island in the Bay of Naples
CO is the abbreviation for company
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A notice on a resort island announces that a company needs seamen.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted sign looks like the definition's content, but 'Sign' alone means a zodiac sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Capricorn, the goat, is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac in astrology.

clue.text: Girl involving soldiers in unarmed combat

indicators.note: involving means the girl's name wraps round the soldiers

blocks.note: a girl's name
RA is the Royal Artillery

explanation.surface: A young woman gets mixed up with troops in a hand-to-hand fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Karate is a Japanese martial art of fighting with hands and feet, without weapons.

clue.text: Told us he had nice recollection of dreaming

indicators.note: read as re-collection, the words are gathered up again in a new order

blocks.note: fifteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tells us they have a pleasant memory of a dream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recollection' looks like memory, but split as re-collection it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with this phrase applied is lost in daydreams, absent-minded and out of touch with reality.

clue.text: Film you abroad, mindless of something Julius said

blocks.note: E.T. is Spielberg's film
French or Latin for you
brute as an adjective means lacking reason

explanation.surface: A foreign film is criticised as thoughtless about some line of Caesar's.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare gives Julius Caesar the Latin words 'and you, Brutus?' as he is stabbed by his friend.

clue.text: Saw notice on time

blocks.note: an ad is an advertisement, a notice
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone spotted a notice about the time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the past of see; it is the noun for an old saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old proverb or maxim, the same thing as a traditional saying.

clue.text: Doctors deny ear ached

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so these words are altered into another order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Physicians dismiss a patient's earache complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctors' reads as physicians, but it is a verb meaning falsifies.
explanation.definitionFit: To ache for something is to long for it, the same as to yearn.

clue.text: Fish arrive on deck

blocks.note: the gar is a long-snouted fish
to land is to arrive

explanation.surface: A caught fish arrives flapping onto a ship's deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deck' looks like the floor of a ship; here it is a verb meaning adorn.
explanation.definitionFit: To garland is to decorate with wreaths of flowers, just as to deck is to adorn.

clue.text: Finally you can return to group

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the next word
return means the word for can is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: the final letter of you
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: An invitation to come back and rejoin the gang at last.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a single group of people or things forming part of a larger whole.

clue.text: Turn and hide glass

blocks.note: to wind is to turn, as a handle
to screen is to conceal

explanation.surface: Instructions to spin round and conceal a drinking vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The windscreen is the pane at the front of a car, a sheet of glass for the driver.

clue.text: Poor writer found on river boat

blocks.note: a pen is a writing instrument
the Nile is the great African river
SS is steamship

explanation.surface: A struggling author is discovered aboard a river steamer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without a penny to their name is destitute, which is to be very poor.

clue.text: FBI agents in radio division

indicators.note: in places the agents within the word for a radio

blocks.note: G-men is slang for agents of the American federal bureau
a radio is a wireless set

explanation.surface: Federal agents are working in a radio unit of the bureau.
explanation.definitionFit: A segment is one of the parts something is divided into, so a section or division.

clue.text: Japan? Go around mid-April

indicators.note: mid- asks for the centre letter of the month named
around means the word for go is wrapped about that letter

blocks.note: to vanish is to go, disappear
the middle letter of the five-letter month

explanation.surface: A suggestion to travel to Japan in the middle of April.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Japan' is a verb here: to coat with a hard black lacquer; the question mark flags the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Japanning is coating with a glossy lacquer, a kind of varnish, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Austrian is even drunk around half nine!

indicators.note: half asks for two of the four letters of the number
drunk means these words stagger into a new order
around means the rearranged letters surround the half number

blocks.note: taken as written
the second half of nine

explanation.surface: A man from Austria is already tipsy by half past nine.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange IS EVEN as VIENSE and put the last half of nine, NE, in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Viennese describes someone from Vienna, the capital of Austria, so an Austrian by birth.

clue.text: I'm getting staff to admit it's rude

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the staff takes the next word inside

blocks.note: taken as written
a pole is a staff or stick
taken as written

explanation.surface: A boss confesses to being discourteous to their employees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' reads as employees, but it means a pole.
explanation.definitionFit: Being impolite means lacking good manners, which is being rude or discourteous to people.

clue.text: Exhausted class getting everything shipshape

blocks.note: all in is informal for tired out
an order is a class, as in biology

explanation.surface: A worn-out class of pupils manages to tidy everything up.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a situation where all things are neat, correct and properly arranged.

clue.text: Strange allure of Hardy's partner

indicators.note: strange letters are oddly arranged, so they should be reordered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The odd attraction of a famous comedian's sidekick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardy' could be the novelist Thomas Hardy, but here it is Oliver Hardy of the comedy double act.
explanation.definitionFit: Stan Laurel paired with Oliver Hardy in the classic film comedy duo Laurel and Hardy.

clue.text: Beat soundly

blocks.note: surface reading: thrash someone thoroughly
setter's reading: a beat in the world of sound, the regular pulse of music

explanation.walkthrough: 'Soundly' looks like it means thoroughly, but it means in sound, turning the violent beat into a musical one.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhythm is the regular pattern of beats in music, a pulse heard in sound.

clue.text: Impressive record once in charge

blocks.note: an EP, extended play, is an old-fashioned record format
i/c is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A record that was once in charge of the charts sounds remarkable.
explanation.definitionFit: Epic, as an adjective, describes something grand, heroic or on a remarkably large scale.

clue.text: Something inevitable about an Andrew Lloyd Weber musical?

indicators.note: something of a word is a part of it, so a run of its letters is wanted

blocks.note: letters three to seven of this word

explanation.surface: A wry question: is there an air of inevitability about one of Lloyd Webber's shows?
explanation.walkthrough: The composer's name is misspelt in the clue; it is Webber.
explanation.definitionFit: Evita is the Lloyd Webber and Rice musical about Eva Peron of Argentina.

clue.text: Impartially point to two students in dock

indicators.note: in places the students inside the word for dock

blocks.note: E, east, is a compass point
a quay is a dock or wharf
L for learner, twice

explanation.surface: A judge fairly directs two students standing in the dock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dock' suggests a courtroom with two accused, but it is the harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Treating everyone equally means giving no side preference, which is acting without bias.

clue.text: New look for an old composer

blocks.note: novel means new
lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: A designer offers a new look for a vintage musician.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivor Novello was a Welsh composer and actor of the early twentieth century, famous for musicals.

clue.text: Enclose in very big launches

indicators.note: in puts the enclosure within the letters for very big

blocks.note: OS is outsize, a clothing label
to pen is to shut in

explanation.surface: Someone shuts away very large rockets.
explanation.definitionFit: To open a show or business is to start it, which is what launching it means.

clue.text: Was unwilling to go outside, one man said

indicators.note: outside means the word for said goes round the number one

blocks.note: he is a male pronoun
stated means said
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: One man explained that he was reluctant to step out of doors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To go outside' reads as a single phrase, but 'outside' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To hesitate is to pause before acting, being reluctant or slow to proceed.
